market_name: Will OpenAI’s market cap be $1.5T or greater at market close on IPO day?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any OpenAI IPO headline (S-1 filing, banker mandate, valuation leak) accompanies the probability move; without a hard catalyst treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT move to QQQ/SMH to see if any move is idiosyncratic to AI-stake names vs broad beta.
time_plan.2h: Re-check the Polymarket implied probability for stability/reversal; a mean-reverting swing signals thin-market noise not information.
time_plan.6h: Scan newswires (Reuters/Bloomberg) for confirmed OpenAI IPO or valuation news; absent that, downgrade any signal.
time_plan.12h: Assess whether MSFT closed with abnormal return vs sector; log outcome and note whether the prediction-market move preceded any public confirmation.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft holds a large economic stake in OpenAI, so a sharp move in the implied probability of a $1.5T+ OpenAI IPO valuation could be read as a mark-up of Microsoft's embedded AI asset value. But this market resolves on a first-trading-day close of an IPO that has not been scheduled and could be a year-plus away, so a probability shift carries almost no near-term (12h) cash-flow or information content for MSFT. The link is real but extremely diffuse and long-dated; any 12h co-movement would be dominated by broad tech/AI sentiment rather than this specific market.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether the probability move coincides with any concrete AI-capex or OpenAI news; otherwise treat as unrelated.
time_plan.1h: Check NVDA and SMH intraday vs SPX beta to isolate any AI-specific bid.
time_plan.2h: Monitor whether prediction-market shift persists or reverses; thin market implies low signal.
time_plan.6h: Look for corroborating funding/valuation reports on OpenAI; absent them, discount.
time_plan.12h: Record SMH close vs benchmark and note whether the prediction market led any public information.

predictions.reasoning: A higher implied OpenAI IPO valuation reflects bullish AI-capex expectations, which broadly benefits semiconductor names (Nvidia, etc.) that supply compute. But this is a very weak, indirect proxy: the market is about a distant, unscheduled listing and its resolution is binary on a single day's close. Any 12h move in SMH would overwhelmingly reflect macro/rates/earnings flow, not this specific probability shift. Included only to note the direction of the thematic tail, not because it is tradable.

evidence_used: Market question concerns OpenAI's first-trading-day market cap ($1.5T+ threshold) on an IPO that is not yet scheduled and may not occur before end-2026
Microsoft is the largest external stakeholder in OpenAI, giving a fundamental but diffuse linkage
AI-capex optimism generically supports semiconductor names like Nvidia (SMH)
Resolution can be 'No IPO by December 31, 2026', underscoring the long and uncertain time horizon
uncertainty_notes: The event horizon (up to end-2026) is wholly mismatched with the 12h prediction window, so near-term asset co-movement is unlikely to be causal
OpenAI is private; there is no direct tradable instrument, forcing weak proxy exposure
Polymarket for a distant, unscheduled IPO is likely thin and noisy, so probability swings may be liquidity artifacts
Even a genuine valuation re-rating for OpenAI would be a small fraction of MSFT's or SMH's total value

llm_justification.summary: This market prices whether a not-yet-scheduled OpenAI IPO would close its first day at $1.5T+ valuation, with a resolution horizon stretching to end-2026. There is no direct tradable instrument, and the only fundamental linkages — Microsoft's OpenAI stake and broad AI-capex sentiment (semiconductors) — are diffuse and long-dated. A sharp probability move here has minimal causal content for any liquid asset over a 12h window; expected moves are well below the 700bps tradable threshold. Direction is best labeled unclear with low confidence.
key_assumptions: No concrete OpenAI IPO catalyst (S-1, banker mandate, priced deal) accompanies the probability move
The prediction market is thin, making probability shifts noisy
MSFT and SMH remain the least-weak available public proxies for OpenAI valuation sentiment
failure_modes: The move reverses quickly, revealing it as thin-market noise rather than information
Any OpenAI valuation news is already public and fully priced into MSFT/SMH, so no residual signal
The proxies are only weakly exposed — OpenAI's implied value is a tiny fraction of MSFT/SMH market cap, so even a correct directional read produces sub-threshold moves
The 12h window is far too short for a resolution event that may be months or years away, breaking any causal mapping
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
